tagline: Ask every row a question, test better wording, and keep the evidence

examples.prompt: I tried two versions of our urgency question in Question Lab and kept the review. Read the rows and my notes, help me choose the clearer wording, and retain it in sheet.json before running the whole file.
examples.caption: Frozen rows, paired answers, full probabilities and your judgment in a portable trial packet

examples.prompt: I dropped my app reviews export on the pane. Read a sample of it, then work out what people complain about most, who is thinking of leaving, and how angry they are. Write me a findings report with the counts and word-for-word quotes.
examples.caption: 1,200 reviews, three questions, 36 seconds, 3 cents: the 119 who may leave. The reviews shown are made up

examples.prompt: Our survey export is in survey.csv with 3,000 free-text answers. Code every answer by theme, tell me the top five themes among the unhappy customers, and list the 20 answers I should read myself.
examples.caption: The agent writes the questions with you, Jev answers them for every row, and the review line shows what to read

examples.prompt: tickets.csv is last month of support tickets. Send each one to a team, flag the urgent ones, and tell me which three problems cost us the most tickets. Save the result so I can open it in Excel.
examples.caption: Every row gets an answer and a confidence. answers.csv is yours to keep
